common_name: Sugar Buns Sweet Corn (Early Cool-Soil Sugary-Enhanced Hybrid)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost when soil reaches at least 60 degrees; Sugar Buns germinates more reliably in cooler soil than many sugary-enhanced corn varieties, allowing an earlier first planting in the Gulf South's spring corn window.

directions: Sow seed 1 inch deep in warm soil, planting in blocks of several short rows rather than one long row to ensure good pollination; Sugar Buns is an early, sugary-enhanced (se) yellow sweet corn valued for reliable germination in cooler soil than many other sweet corn types tolerate well, letting Gulf Coast gardeners get a jump on the spring planting window. It produces 7-inch ears with tender, sweet, deep yellow kernels that hold their eating quality well for several days after picking. Feed with nitrogen and water deeply during tasseling and ear fill, since drought stress at this stage causes poorly filled ears. Harvest when silks have browned and kernels are plump and release a milky juice when pressed.
